data.name: Neon Shadow
data.detailed_description:
Neon Shadow is a fast paced Cyber Punk FPS inspired by classic shooters. Suit up and grab your shotgun. Your mission: Save humanity from the dark mechanoids who have taken control of your space station and soon the rest of the galaxy!
Everything in the Steam version has been improved from the controls to the graphics, we would like to think of it as Neon Shadow 2.0. Please shout if there are additional features you would like to see!
Planned additions so far are; split-screen up to 4, chat functions, player names (over head) and Tobii support.

Features:
• Multiplayer.
• Old school first person shooter game-play.
• Single player campaign.
• Online multiplayer death-match mode
• LAN multiplayer death-match.
• Cyber Punk soundtrack from Abducted by Sharks.

reviews.review:
Neon Shadow is an unapologetically old-school first-person shooter that channels the spirit of genre staples from the 1990s while layering its action with a sleek science-fiction presentation. Developed by Tasty Poison and published by Crescent Moon Games, the title places players aboard a futuristic space station overrun by hostile mechanical forces threatening humanity's survival. Rather than attempting to reinvent the FPS formula, Neon Shadow embraces the fundamentals: move quickly, shoot everything in sight, and survive long enough to reach the next objective. Its straightforward approach may feel refreshing to players who have grown tired of increasingly complicated modern shooters.

The game's campaign wastes little time introducing its world. Players assume the role of a soldier tasked with eliminating a machine uprising spreading through a massive orbital facility. Storytelling remains deliberately minimal, serving primarily as a backdrop for the action. While there are no dramatic twists or deeply developed characters, the setting succeeds in establishing a tense atmosphere. The space station's corridors are filled with flickering lights, metallic architecture, and neon accents that create a distinctive cyberpunk identity. This visual style helps elevate the experience beyond its simple premise and gives the game a memorable personality.

Combat is where Neon Shadow shines brightest. Every encounter emphasizes speed and momentum, encouraging players to stay mobile while weaving through enemy fire. Weapons are easy to understand but satisfying to use, ranging from rapid-fire firearms to heavier options capable of clearing groups of enemies in seconds. The game rarely slows its pace, maintaining a steady rhythm that keeps players engaged from one level to the next. Its design philosophy clearly draws inspiration from classic arena shooters, rewarding quick reflexes and aggressive tactics over cover-based gameplay or lengthy tactical planning.

Despite originally being developed for mobile devices, the Steam version adapts surprisingly well to PC. Controls feel responsive, and the enhanced presentation makes the transition to desktop gaming largely successful. The environments, while not especially complex, feature enough visual variety to prevent monotony. Neon-lit hallways, industrial chambers, and mechanical facilities all contribute to the sensation of progressing deeper into an occupied station. Accompanying the visuals is an energetic soundtrack that complements the action effectively, adding intensity to firefights without overpowering the experience.

The inclusion of multiplayer options also adds value. Online and LAN deathmatch modes extend the game's lifespan beyond the single-player campaign, offering opportunities for competitive matches that fit naturally with Neon Shadow's fast-paced mechanics. Although finding active online opponents may be challenging due to the game's age, the feature remains a welcome addition and reinforces the title's commitment to recreating the feel of classic shooters. Players who enjoy local multiplayer sessions will appreciate having additional ways to experience the game beyond the campaign.

However, Neon Shadow is not without limitations. The campaign is relatively short, and seasoned FPS fans may complete it in a single sitting. Enemy types can become repetitive over time, and some level layouts reveal the game's modest budget and mobile origins. Those expecting an expansive narrative adventure or cutting-edge visuals may come away disappointed. Nevertheless, the game understands its strengths and focuses on delivering concise, arcade-style entertainment rather than overstretching its ambitions.

Ultimately, Neon Shadow succeeds because it remains committed to its identity. It is a compact, energetic shooter that respects the classics while presenting them through a futuristic lens. Its combination of rapid-fire gameplay, stylish environments, and multiplayer support makes it an enjoyable experience for fans of retro-inspired FPS titles. While it lacks the depth and scope of larger releases, it offers several hours of entertaining action that capture the essence of a bygone era of gaming.

Rating: 7/10
